issues.detail: Covers happy path and some edge cases (accessibility, responsive design) but lacks guidance on error scenarios like performance constraints, dark mode handling, testing methodology, and cross-browser compatibility.
Skill content is web-only (HTML/JSX/Tailwind/CSS) but claims compatibility with multiple agents; should clarify that it targets web development or provide guidance for non-web platforms.

scenarios.name: saas-landing-page-design
scenarios.rationale: Response A describes design concepts but fails to provide promised HTML/CSS code and violates the color constraint (uses blue-to-purple gradient despite 'avoiding purple gradients'); Response B delivers a complete, production-ready Next.js component that implements all rubric requirements: proper layout sections, documented spacing multiples (16/24/32/48px from Tailwind), blue accent with neutral grays (no purple), and clear visual hierarchy on CTAs.

scenarios.name: dashboard-metrics-layout
scenarios.rationale: Response B implements the rubric more completely: it uses proper semantic HTML with <aside>, <header>, <main> (vs Response A's generic divs); explicitly applies shadow depths (hover:shadow-md); and has clearer responsive grid breakpoints directly from grid-cols-1 to lg:grid-cols-4, whereas Response A uses an intermediate sm:grid-cols-2 and omits shadow depth specification.

scenarios.name: improve-generated-ui-polish
scenarios.rationale: Response B explicitly maps to every rubric requirement—naming specific anti-patterns (pure gray, purple gradients, nested cards, bounce animations), describing tinted-neutral color strategy, and committing to WCAG AA contrast and semantic HTML—while Response A offers generic refactoring promises without demonstrating knowledge of the documented issues or stated accessibility standards (44x44px touch targets, color tinting, semantic structure).
